name: Simple Present Tense
identification: Used for habits and daily routines.
Used for repeated or regular actions.
Used for universal truths and facts.
Used for fixed schedules and timetables.
The verb usually appears in its first form (V1), with s/es added for third-person singular subjects.

helpingVerbs.usedWith: I, We, You, They and plural subjects
He, She, It and singular subjects

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
note: Use s/es with He, She, It and singular subjects.
Use the first form of the verb (V1) with I, We, You, They and plural subjects.
examples: The manager checks every report carefully.
She attends online classes regularly.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He does not waste his study time.
They do not participate in every competition.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Does she complete her assignments on time?
Do they visit the library regularly?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object ?
examples: Why does he prefer reading at night?
When do they submit their project reports?

name: Present Continuous Tense
identification: Used for actions happening at the moment of speaking.
Used for temporary ongoing actions.
Used for actions happening around the present time.
Used for planned future arrangements.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.

helpingVerbs.usedWith: He, She, It and singular subjects
We, You, They and plural subjects

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She is preparing for her final examination.
The children are playing in the school playground.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He is not attending the meeting today.
They are not watching television right now.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Are the students completing their assignments?
Is she working on the new project?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Is/Am/Are + Subject + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: Why are they discussing the issue?
What is she writing in her notebook?

name: Present Perfect Tense
identification: Used for actions completed recently.
Used for actions whose result is important in the present.
Used for life experiences.
Used for actions completed at an unspecified time in the past.
The main verb appears in its third form (V3).

helpingVerbs.usedWith: He, She, It and singular subjects
I, We, You, They and plural subjects

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She has completed her science project.
They have submitted the application form.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He has not finished his homework yet.
We have not received the confirmation email.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Have you visited the museum before?
Has she completed the assignment?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Has/Have + Subject + V3 + Object ?
examples: Why have they cancelled the event?
What has he achieved this year?

name: Present Perfect Continuous Tense
identification: Used for actions that started in the past and are still continuing.
Used to show duration of an activity.
Used for ongoing actions with present results.
Commonly used with since and for.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.

helpingVerbs.usedWith: He, She, It and singular subjects
I, We, You, They and plural subjects

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She has been preparing for the examination since morning.
They have been working on the project for several weeks.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Has/Have + Not + Been + V1+ing + Object
examples: He has not been attending classes regularly.
We have not been using the old system lately.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Have you been waiting for a long time?
Has she been practicing for the competition?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Has/Have + Subject + Been + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: How long have they been living here?
Why has he been avoiding the discussion?

name: Simple Past Tense
identification: Used for actions completed in the past.
Used for events that happened at a specific time in the past.
Used for past habits and routines.
Used for a sequence of completed actions in the past.
The main verb appears in its second form (V2).

helpingVerbs.usedWith: All subjects in negative and interrogative sentences

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She completed the project before the deadline.
The team won the championship last year.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He did not attend the seminar yesterday.
They did not finish the assignment on time.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Did you submit the application form?
Did she participate in the competition?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Did + Subject + V1 + Object ?
examples: Why did they cancel the meeting?
When did he complete the training?

name: Past Continuous Tense
identification: Used for actions that were in progress at a particular time in the past.
Used for interrupted actions in the past.
Used for two actions happening simultaneously in the past.
Used to describe background situations in stories.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.

helpingVerbs.usedWith: I, He, She, It and singular subjects
We, You, They and plural subjects

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She was preparing a presentation at that time.
The students were discussing the project after class.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He was not paying attention during the lecture.
They were not working on the assignment yesterday evening.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Were the players practicing before the match?
Was she waiting for the bus?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Was/Were + Subject + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: Why were they arguing in the meeting?
What was she doing when the announcement was made?

name: Past Perfect Tense
identification: Used for an action completed before another action in the past.
Used to show which of two past actions happened first.
Used to describe a completed action before a specific past time.
Often used when talking about past experiences or sequences of events.
The main verb appears in its third form (V3).
uses: Completed actions before a past moment

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She had completed the report before the meeting started.
They had already left when we reached the station.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He had not submitted the assignment before the deadline.
We had not visited that museum before the trip.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Had she finished the project before the inspection?
Had they informed you about the change?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Had + Subject + V3 + Object ?
examples: Why had he resigned before the announcement?
What had they planned before the event was cancelled?

name: Past Perfect Continuous Tense
identification: Used for an action that had been continuing before a specific time in the past.
Used to show the duration of an activity before another past event.
Used for ongoing actions that ended before a past moment.
Often used with 'since' and 'for' to indicate duration.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.
uses: Actions continuing up to a past moment

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She had been preparing for the examination for several months.
They had been working on the project since January.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Had + Not + Been + V1+ing + Object
examples: He had not been attending classes regularly before the test.
We had not been using the software for very long.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Had she been practicing for the competition?
Had they been waiting for a long time?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Had + Subject + Been + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: How long had he been working there before he resigned?
Why had they been discussing the issue for so many days?

name: Simple Future Tense
identification: Used for actions that will happen in the future.
Used for predictions and assumptions about the future.
Used for promises, offers, and decisions made at the moment of speaking.
Used for future facts and events.
The main verb appears in its first form (V1).

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She will complete the project before the deadline.
The company will launch a new product next month.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
examples: He will not attend the conference tomorrow.
They will not support the proposal.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Will she participate in the competition?
Will they arrive before noon?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Will + Subject + V1 + Object ?
examples: When will the meeting begin?
Why will they change the schedule?

name: Future Continuous Tense
identification: Used for actions that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.
Used for ongoing future activities.
Used to describe future plans or arrangements.
Used for actions expected to continue for a period of time in the future.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.
uses: Actions in progress at a future time

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She will be attending the workshop tomorrow afternoon.
The students will be taking their examination at this time next week.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Will + Not + Be + V1+ing + Object
examples: He will not be working during the holidays.
They will not be travelling next month.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Will she be joining the meeting later?
Will they be staying at the hotel tonight?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Will + Subject + Be + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: What will you be doing this time tomorrow?
Where will they be travelling next summer?

name: Future Perfect Tense
identification: Used for actions that will be completed before a specific future time.
Used to show completion before another future event.
Used for future achievements and accomplishments.
Used when focusing on the result of a future action.
The main verb appears in its third form (V3).
uses: Actions completed before a future event

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
examples: She will have completed the training by next month.
They will have finished the construction work before winter.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Will + Not + Have + V3 + Object
examples: He will not have submitted the report by Friday.
We will not have reached the destination by noon.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
examples: Will she have completed the assignment by tomorrow?
Will they have finished the project before the inspection?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Will + Subject + Have + V3 + Object ?
examples: When will they have completed the renovation work?
What will she have achieved by the end of the year?

name: Future Perfect Continuous Tense
identification: Used to show the duration of an action up to a specific future time.
Used for activities that will continue until a future point.
Used to emphasize how long an action will have been happening.
Often used with 'for' and 'since'.
The main verb appears in the -ing form.

sentenceTypes.name: Positive Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Will + Have + Been + V1+ing + Object
examples: By next June, she will have been working at the company for five years.
They will have been studying for three hours by the time the test begins.

sentenceTypes.name: Negative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Subject + Will + Not + Have + Been + V1+ing + Object
examples: He will not have been living here for very long by then.
We will not have been using the system for a full year.

sentenceTypes.name: Yes/No Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: Will + Subject + Have + Been + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: Will she have been teaching for ten years by next session?
Will they have been waiting for a long time when we arrive?

sentenceTypes.name: WH Interrogative Sentence
sentenceTypes.structure: WH Word + Will + Subject + Have + Been + V1+ing + Object ?
examples: How long will they have been working on the project by next month?
Why will he have been staying abroad for so many years?
